content:
paging-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: high GPU memory pressure observed on runtime pool eu-west-1-gpu-02 — potential KV cache paging. Severity: P1. Root thread created 2491234567

alice (oncall): seeing elevated latency from Hosted API, error spikes in 502s and OOM traces. Customer impact: recent spike in retries for chat endpoints.

ben (sre): pulling logs now. Quick check: any recent deploys?

carla (runtime-eng): no deploys in the last 3 hours. Rolling back nothing. Hypothesis1: KV cache fragmentation leading to pages being moved to host and causing GPU OOM cascade. Hypothesis2: large-batch job (external) hitting a node and starving others due to slab allocation.

dan (eng-ml): can we get per-GPU slab / page stats from the runtime? need `nvidia-smi` and our allocator dumps.

carla (runtime-eng): grabbing stats — gimme 30s. Running `kubectl exec` to collect `nvidia-smi -q` and `runtimectl dump-mem --kv=pages` across affected pods.

paging-bot: Incident timeline entry: 2491234500 - alert threshold breached; 2491234562 - first 502 observed; 2491234567 - paging-bot created thread.

carla (runtime-eng): paste logs below (trimmed):
```
GPU 0: 31.7 GiB total, 31.6 GiB used
Processes: runtime_server (pid 3121) 99% mem
Allocator: slab_count=8123, slab_frag=18.2%, kv_pages=1243, kv_swap_out=216
2026-03-15T10:02:14Z runtime ERROR: OOM while allocating 96MB for attention_kv cache
```

ben (sre): interesting slab_frag 18% — that can cause right-sized allocations to fail if large contiguous blocks needed. Any recent model variant changes?

carla (runtime-eng): no model changes. But we have a traffic surge for a customer service bot — many long context prompts. That increases KV cache retention.

ed (customer-success): customer X reported 5-10% failed requests for chat in EU around 10:02 UTC. They're starting to escalate.

alice (oncall): mitigation plan (live): 1) reduce default batch_size for chat route from 8 -> 4, 2) enable immediate KV eviction policy on affected nodes, 3) route new requests to eu-west-1-gpu-03 (lower-util) if capacity allows, 4) scale up pool by +1 node if autoscaling can't keep up. Agree?

frank (prodops): scaling requested — +1 node provisioning now (estimated 3m). Routing change: adding temporary weighted route to gw to favor -03.

carla (runtime-eng): applying KV eviction: `runtimectl set-evict --policy aggressive --threshold 60%` on the three affected pods. Also dropping `max_seq_len` for in-flight sessions > 8192 to 4096 where safe.

ben (sre): I want to capture a heap profile before aggressive eviction fully clears — can you snapshot `runtimectl heap-snapshot --path=/tmp/heap-249123` then evict?

carla (runtime-eng): done. Snapshot saved and uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-incident-dumps/2491234567/heap-249123.json

carla (runtime-eng): eviction enabled. Observing KV swap_out rate drop and immediate free of ~2.1 GiB on GPU 0.

alice (oncall): customer-impact update: Ed — can you confirm which customers had requests retried and whether we engaged SLOs?

ed (customer-success): customer X saw increased retries, no credit ask yet. I'm drafting a proactive message to the customer explaining we're mitigating and will follow with RCA.

dan (eng-ml): small ask: can we temporarily reduce max batch token length per request or enforce streaming cutoff? Long-context requests are the biggest KV pressure.

carla (runtime-eng): implemented a temporary per-account context cap: `context_max_tokens=6000` for accounts with >1k active sessions. Applied via routing policy config.

paging-bot: New log dump available: /var/log/runtime/containers/3121/oom-trace.log (sha256: abc123). Linked in incident runbook.

ben (sre): aggregating per-node `dmesg` and kernel logs in case of host-side paging: dmesg shows repeated GPU driver pagefaults around 10:02:12 UTC.

carla (runtime-eng): posting allocator debug snippet:
```
[alloc_table] request=98304 bytes, nearest_slab=65536, slabs_free=0 -> attempt_coalesce failed
kv_page_map: 1243 entries, extents=9, largest_free_extent=54MB
```
This suggests fragmentation: many small free slabs but no contiguous block for KV allocation.

ben (sre): agreed fragmentation looks real. For medium term we should run defragmentation sweep on slack nodes and prioritize allocation for KV on new nodes to reduce pressure.

alice (oncall): can we get a count of top offending sessions (largest KV footprints) to identify noisy tenants?

carla (runtime-eng): running `runtimectl top-kv-sessions --limit 20` -> returning around 3 sessions holding 60% of KV pages (session ids redacted). Opening a followup ticket to customer-success to identify mapping.

ed (customer-success): confirming — those sessions map to customer X and an internal test harness. I'll reach out to customer X to ask them to throttle long historical contexts for the next hour.

frank (prodops): scale up completed: new node joined pool at 2491234723. Routing now balancing.

paging-bot: Update: severity downgraded to P2 at 2491234790 after eviction and scale. Continued monitoring.

carla (runtime-eng): post-eviction stats:
```
GPU 0: 31.7 GiB total, 25.0 GiB used
slab_count=7810, slab_frag=7.9%, kv_pages=621, kv_swap_out=12
```

ben (sre): slab_frag down to 7.9% — good sign. We still need to run maintenance defrag job in staging to test heuristics.

alice (oncall): next actions (in-thread RCA coordination): 1) collect full timeline & attach logs (Ben), 2) run defrag candidate in staging and measure tail-latency (Carla), 3) customer outreach note & follow-ups (Ed), 4) create postmortem draft and hypothesis list (Alice). Assign owners and ETA 24h.

carla (runtime-eng): I'll prepare a short repro script to stress KV cache and test different slab alloc strategies. Will post results in this thread.

ben (sre): uploaded aggregated logs and dmesg to s3://redwood-incident-dumps/2491234567/aggregated.tar.gz

ed (customer-success): I've sent an interim message to customer X and offered a call if they want details. Keeping them updated.

alice (oncall): handing off to ben for overnight watch. Ben — take primary on follow-up and update the incident timeline. I'll be available for questions.

ben (sre): taking oncall handoff. I'll keep monitoring metrics and will post updates in the next 2h or earlier if anything flares.

carla (runtime-eng): quick note for RCA: potential remediation candidates — adaptive slab coalescing, per-session soft caps, and smarter eviction that favors extremely large KV sessions first. Will evaluate perf tradeoffs.

alice (oncall): thanks all. Closing live mitigation loop — will keep thread open for RCA notes. :white_check_mark:

paging-bot: Incident timeline snapshot saved to runbook 2491234567-runbook.md

ben (sre): last check: tail error rate now ~0.3% (baseline 0.1%). We'll track.

carla (runtime-eng): attaching quick perf graph of token latency pre/post eviction (link): https://grafana.redwood.company/d/xyz/kv-paging?from=2491234400&to=2491235000

ed (customer-success): customer X acknowledged receipt and appreciates the quick mitigation. They asked for a post-incident RCA once ready.

ben (sre): logging final note for handoff: cause hypothesis = KV cache fragmentation + concentrated long-context sessions; immediate remediation = aggressive eviction + scale + routing; medium-term = defrag sweeps and allocator changes.

carla (runtime-eng): will start a PR with defrag change and add canary tests in staging.

alice (oncall): thread timestamp 2491234567. I'll post the postmortem draft in 24-48h. Good job team.
